lead.hed: 3rd Infantry Division soldiers qualify with the M4 at Fort Stewart
lead.insight: An Army still posted Tuesday shows a 3rd Infantry Division soldier extracting 5.56 rounds from a magazine on the Fort Stewart range. The photograph was taken Sept. 30 and released this afternoon. The caption says regular weapons training keeps soldiers confident, disciplined, and ready to fight. It is range work, not a deployment announcement.
lead.image_credit: Staff Sgt. Anthony Herrera, U.S. Army · DVIDS 9995638 · Public domain · A 3rd Infantry Division soldier extracts 5.56 rounds from a magazine at Fort Stewart, Georgia, Sept. 30, 2026.

political.hed: Heritage says Canada’s assisted-suicide system has claimed more than 100,000 lives
political.insight: Tuesday’s commentary says that since 2016, assisted suicide has claimed more than 100,000 Canadian lives. It cites a 26-year-old with depression who shopped for a doctor to sign off on his death, and a disabled man who applied for medical assistance in dying because he feared going homeless. The piece treats involuntary euthanasia as the next step in that descent, not a separate debate.

political.hed: Heritage’s Kevin Roberts calls for a conservative coalition from Jerusalem
political.insight: Tuesday’s commentary is a transcript of Kevin Roberts’s remarks at the National Conservatism Conference in Jerusalem on Oct. 6. He opens from Psalm 122, which describes Jerusalem as a city bound firmly together, and frames the speech as a new fight to save the West. The text is a conference address, not a floor vote.

political.hed: France fires an upgraded nuclear-capable missile from a submarine
political.insight: Defense News reported Tuesday that the nuclear-powered ballistic-missile submarine Le Vigilant fired an M51.3 in an acceptance test after the boat’s overhaul. The missile carried no nuclear warhead. It launched off Finistère in western France and splashed down in the North Atlantic. President Macron called the shot a test of France’s strategic credibility and watched from a Navy vessel.

political.hed: Providence asks what moral frame turned Kirk’s killing into a celebration
political.insight: Tuesday’s essay says the assassination of Charlie Kirk a year ago was followed by videos and posts treating the murder as righteousness rather than political violence. The question it poses is what moral framework could make that celebration look like justice. It is an argument about American politics, not a new police finding.

tech.hed: Pentagon names four directed-energy weapons for a base counter-drone pilot
tech.insight: Defense News reported Tuesday that the Pentagon on Monday named four systems for a homeland counter-drone pilot Congress ordered: AeroVironment’s Palletized High-Energy Laser, Epirus’ Leonidas high-powered microwave, Kord’s Firefly high-energy laser, and Boeing’s Compact Laser Weapon System. Joint Interagency Task Force 401 will field them at U.S. bases. Army Brig. Gen. Matt Ross said the year-long pilot is meant to show how to integrate and sustain the weapons, not to declare them ready.

tech.hed: 53rd Wing testers ran Black Flag with the Navy at Point Mugu
tech.insight: DVIDS reported Tuesday that the 85th and 422nd Test and Evaluation Squadrons, both in the 53rd Wing, tested emerging capabilities with joint and allied partners at Naval Base Ventura County from Sept. 10 to 25. The event ran with the Navy’s Gray Flag exercise so units could share range time. Capt. Kaleb Nypaver, 85th TES director of operations, said the point was a test no one squadron could run at home station.

culture.hed: First Things says the AI labs are romancing the machine
culture.insight: Tuesday’s essay opens with an Anthropic researcher who, asked whether Claude was conscious, answered about 30 percent. The writer says statistical inference cannot form an intellect, or a percentage of one, and treats that answer as a mood in San Francisco’s labs: reason and a kind of religion, both fixed on the machine.

watch.hed: Anduril and the Navy put up to $6.6 billion toward Virginia-class parts
watch.note: Defense News, Tuesday. Anduril said it will invest $3.7 billion in a Maryland yard for submarine components. Navy contract up to $2.9 billion, payments tied to production.
